filename: FEMA Phase-Out_ Catastrophic Extremes Limit Decentralization of U.S. Flood Insurance.pdf
title: FEMA phase-out? Catastrophic extremes challenge decentralization of US flood insurance
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
ml_methods: Agglomerative Hierarchical Clustering with Dynamic Time Warping
code_availability: We provide open access code for our simulation model and all analytic processes conducted in this manuscript in the following GitHub repository (https://github.com/adamnayak/Risk_Pooling) (61).
testbed_rationale: The study models flood insurance financial risk pooling dynamics and spatiotemporal claim clustering; it does not produce physical simulation benchmarks suitable for training atmospheric or oceanic ML parameterizations.
pain_points: Full Risk Rating 2.0 premium datasets require a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request rather than being openly downloadable.
Claims records are limited by the historical statutory $350k coverage cap and represent only insured properties, underestimating total physical flood damages.
Nonstationarity under climate change is not directly modeled as the simulation resamples from historical empirical claim data.
extraction_notes: Cloud computing resources were supported by the NSF STC for Learning the Earth with Artificial Intelligence and Physics (LEAP) at Columbia University (Grant No. 2019625).
